category_specific_evidence: Special values involved are NaN and +/-inf in the tolerance arguments atol and rtol of np.isclose, not in the data arrays (test_tol_warnings uses inf and nan for atol and rtol with a=[1,2,3]).
The PR title states the bug as allclose not warning for 'invalid value encountered in multiply' and says it alternatively checks validity of tolerances.

The first diff checks np.all(np.isfinite(atol)) and np.all(np.isfinite(rtol)) and, when false, reads np.geterr()['invalid'] and warns with RuntimeWarning, raises FloatingPointError, or prints, depending on the errstate setting.

The test test_tol_warnings iterates atol and rtol over [inf, nan, 1], skips the case where both are 1, and asserts exactly one RuntimeWarning whose message contains 'One of rtol or atol is not valid, atol: {i}, rtol: {j}'.
